newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: KALNAPILIS TO PRODUCE MALT WITH FINNISH FIRM.
newsitem.headline: KALNAPILIS TO PRODUCE MALT WITH FINNISH FIRM.

text.p: Lithuania's Kalnapilis brewery said on Friday that it had signed a joint-venture agreement with Finland's Lahden Polttimo to produce malt.
The beer producer said in a statement that the joint-venture will be called Litmalt and that each partner would have a 50 percent stake in it.
It said that production would begin in June of this year using Kalnapilis' existing malt production lines.
It added that the Finnish partner had agreed to invest 10 million litas in the production lines this year.
Kalnapilis said that it wants to boost its annual malt production turnover to 12,000 tonnes from 9,000 tonnes and that the quality of its malt would improve.
It also said that Litmalt planned to become the biggest malt producer in the Baltic countries and that they would be the main market for its product.
Kalnapilis is 86.3 percent owned by Nordic-based Baltic Beverages Holding.
The company is rapidly expanding in the Lithuanian beer market.
It had a 23.06 percent share of the local beer market in the first quarter of 1997, compared to 21 percent in the same period last year.
Kalnapilis said earlier on Friday that it sold 200,000 decilitres of beer in March of this year versus 170,000 decilitres in February.
